results.title: Marketing Seminar Series | Minnesota Carlson
results.content: **Abstract:** This talk will discuss an ongoing research stream examining how people's political identity affects a variety of consumer decisions such as: education choices, financial risk taking, customer satisfaction, hedonic/utilitarian preferences and so forth. In this paper, we attempt to answer this question using data from an experiment with two novel features: (i) survey information on consumers’ prior brand ownership, familiarity with each brand, and prior experience using different product features, and (ii) eye‐tracking data capturing search behavior at a very granular level. **Abstract:** Research on numerosity demonstrates that consumers’ judgment can be influenced by the scale on which product benefit information is presented. **Abstract:** We estimate the effect of consumer search on the price of the purchased product in a physical store environment. **Who:** Linli Xu, Assistant Professor of Marketing, University of Minnesota - Carlson School of Management. **Who:** Joseph Redden, Assistant Professor of Marketing, University of Minnesota - Carlson School of Management. **Who:** Maria Ana Vitorino, Assistant Professor of Marketing, University of Minnesota - Carlson School of Management.
